- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5) over 5+ days, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward mid-range.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; apply 10–15% downward adjustment for first 7 days if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- If true outcome shows strong downward correction after a high forecast, model may be lagging; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3 days if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.5 and price is rising.
